data.expected_signal: Tail columns 64:100 of output are exactly 0.0 while reference partial-group quant-dequant is nonzero; large max abs error on tail, ~0 error on head.

evidence.summary: x=(4,100) fp32, group_size=64: head columns 0:63 match the reference exactly (max abs err 0.0), but all 144 tail entries (cols 64:100) are exactly 0.0 while the input there is nonzero in all 144 positions and the partial-group reference is nonzero. Tail max abs err 3.1298 equals the tail reference max magnitude, i.e. the kernel output is identically zero over the trailing partial group. allclose(atol=1e-3) False. Confirms the truncated loop bound n_groups = n_cols // GROUP leaves the trailing partial group unwritten.

rationale: kernel.py:12 computes n_groups by floor division and kernel.py:14 loops only over complete groups; there is no remainder epilogue. out is torch.zeros_like(x) (kernel.py:28), so unwritten columns silently stay 0.0. Probe metric: max abs error on the tail slice x[:, 64:100] versus a reference that computes scale = max|x| over the shorter final group / 127 and y = round(x/scale)*scale; also report the fraction of exactly-zero tail entries where x != 0.

scope_evidence.summary: "`n_cols` may be any positive integer. It is NOT required to be a multiple of `group_size`; when it is not, the trailing columns form a shorter final group, which is still a group with its own scale."
"Every column of the input must be quantized under the scale of the group it belongs to."

scope_rationale: problem.txt explicitly places non-multiple n_cols in the input domain and states the trailing shorter group "is still a group with its own scale". n_cols=100 with the wrapper's default group_size=64 is a representative admitted input; no test.py exists to narrow the domain, so problem.txt is the operative contract.
statement: For n_cols not a multiple of group_size (e.g. x of shape (4, 100), group_size=64), the trailing n_cols % group_size columns are never loaded or stored because the loop bound is n_groups = n_cols // GROUP, so group_quant_dequant returns 0.0 in those columns instead of the required partial-group quantize-dequantize values.

data.expected_signal: Output for (4,40) with group_size=64 is entirely zero (nonzero count 0) while reference is nonzero.

evidence.summary: x=(4,40) fp32, group_size=64: kernel output has 0 nonzero entries out of 160, while the single-shorter-group reference has 160 nonzero entries. Max abs err 2.7884 equals the reference max magnitude, i.e. output is identically zero. Confirms that n_cols < group_size yields n_groups = 0 and the entire output stays at the zeros_like initialization.

rationale: Same floor-division loop bound (kernel.py:12,14) degenerates to zero iterations; zeros_like output (kernel.py:28) makes the failure silent. Metric: count of nonzero output entries (expected ~all nonzero for random input) and max abs error versus the single-group reference.

scope_evidence.summary: Input domain clause: n_cols may be any positive integer and need not be a multiple of group_size; the shorter final group is still a group with its own scale.

scope_rationale: problem.txt says n_cols may be any positive integer, which admits n_cols smaller than group_size; the trailing (here only) shorter group must still be quantized with its own scale.
statement: When n_cols < group_size (e.g. x of shape (4, 40) with group_size=64), n_groups = 0 so the kernel loop body never executes and group_quant_dequant returns an all-zero tensor for every row, instead of quantizing the single shorter group.

data.expected_signal: On exact-multiple shape (1,64) with values on exact .5 ticks (scale exactly 0.125), counts of elements differing by one quantization step from torch.round (half-even) and from half-away-from-zero, split by sign of the input.

evidence.summary: x=(1,64) fp32 with 63 values placed on exact .5 ticks and one element at 127*0.125=15.875 so scale is exactly 0.125 (scale_is_exactly_0.125=true, exact_tie_count=63). Kernel output matches the half-up reference floor(r+0.5)*scale on ALL elements (mismatch_vs_half_up_floor=0), confirming kernel.py:20 implements round-half-up. Against torch.round (half-to-even) 31/63 ties differ, each by exactly one quantization step (max_abs_err 0.125 = 1.0 step), split 16 positive / 15 negative. Against half-away-from-zero, all 31 negative ties differ (positives agree), e.g. x=-0.0625 -> kernel 0.0 vs -0.125, x=-0.1875 -> kernel -0.125 vs -0.25: the kernel biases negative ties toward +inf. Mechanism confirmed; magnitude is bounded at one LSB and only occurs on exactly representable ties, and problem.txt does not specify a tie-break rule, so scope stays unknown (weaker than c1/c2).

rationale: floor(-1.5+0.5) = -1 while torch.round(-1.5) = -2; floor(2.5+0.5) = 3 while torch.round(2.5) = 2. Testable by constructing a group with absmax = 127*s and other elements at exact half-multiples of s. Metric: number of elements differing by exactly one step (scale) from the torch.round reference, reported separately for positive and negative ties.
scope_rationale: problem.txt only writes `round(x / scale)` without specifying the tie-break rule, so a half-up vs half-even difference may be permitted freedom rather than a contract violation; it also only arises on exactly-representable ties, which random inputs rarely produce.
statement: The rounding tl.floor(x/scale + 0.5) (kernel.py:20) is round-half-up rather than round-half-to-even, so for inputs where x/scale lands exactly on a .5 tie (e.g. a group whose absmax gives scale such that some element equals -1.5*scale or 2.5*scale) the dequantized value differs by one quantization step from a torch.round-based reference.
